match.reason: The closest bank point, chem-oxidation-numbers, teaches how to assign oxidation numbers and what a rise or fall means, but it does not cover identifying the oxidising agent, the reducing agent or conjugate redox pairs, which the new point requires, so a new point is the safer match.

draft.title: Redox and oxidation numbers
card: Redox reactions transfer electrons. Oxidation is loss of electrons. Reduction is gain of electrons.
An oxidation number tracks electrons in a species. Free elements are 0, simple ions equal their charge, oxygen is usually -2 and hydrogen is usually +1 in compounds.
If an atom's oxidation number rises, it is oxidised. If it falls, it is reduced. A reaction with no change in any oxidation number is not redox.

The reducing agent is the species oxidised, as it gives away electrons. The oxidising agent is the species reduced, as it takes electrons. A conjugate redox pair is an oxidant and the reductant it becomes, such as Cu²⁺ and Cu.
draft.remember: Oxidation number up means oxidised, and that species is the reducing agent.

a.q: In Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s), which species is the reducing agent?
opts: Zn(s), because its oxidation number rises from 0 to +2
Zn(s), because its oxidation number falls from +2 to 0
Cu²⁺(aq), because its oxidation number falls from +2 to 0
Cu²⁺(aq), because its oxidation number rises from 0 to +2
a.why: Zinc goes from 0 to +2, so it is oxidised and gives away electrons. That makes it the reducing agent. Cu²⁺ is tempting because it is involved in the electron transfer, but it is reduced, so it is the oxidising agent.
a.clue: The reducing agent is the one that is oxidised.

b.q: In 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s), which pair is a conjugate redox pair?
b.why: A conjugate pair is an oxidant and the reductant it becomes. Mg²⁺ in MgO is the product of Mg losing electrons, so Mg²⁺ and Mg are a pair. O₂ and Mg are the two reactants, so they are not a pair.
b.clue: A pair is one element in two oxidation states, not two reactants.

a.best: Zn(s), because its oxidation number rises from 0 to +2
